title: Breakfast Sandwich Recall Expands to Texas-Made Items Sold in Seven States, Including Texas
excerpt: Fresh & Ready Foods has expanded its recall of breakfast sandwiches over possible Listeria contamination to include products made at its Longview, Texas,…
content:
Fresh & Ready Foods has expanded its recall of breakfast sandwiches over possible Listeria contamination to include products made at its Longview, Texas, facility and sold in seven states, including Texas, federal officials said.

The company announced the expansion Nov. 17, and the Food and Drug Administration posted the notice Nov. 18. The added products were made with biscuits from C.H. Guenther & Son of San Antonio, which recalled certain biscuit products over possible contamination with Listeria monocytogenes.

What is recalled

The newly added products were produced at Fresh & Ready Foods' Longview, Texas, facility and distributed between Oct. 15 and Nov. 11 through employee break rooms, Grab & Go coolers, refrigerated vending machines and micro-markets:

  • Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich, 5.7 ounces, in clear plastic film, with "Fresh Thru" dates of Nov. 12 to Nov. 22, sold in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas.
  • Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy, 9.5 ounces, in a clear clamshell, with expiration dates of Nov. 12 to Nov. 18, sold in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service issued a public health alert Nov. 14 for ready-to-eat meat items made with the recalled biscuits, including the gravy product. The expansion follows the company's Nov. 8 recall of 2,414 sausage, egg and cheese sandwiches made at its Renton, Washington, facility.

Why it matters

Listeria monocytogenes can cause serious and sometimes fatal infections in young children, frail or elderly people, and others with weakened immune systems. In pregnant women, it can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery or life-threatening infection of the newborn.

No illnesses have been reported to date in connection with the recalled products, according to the company and federal officials.

What to do

Consumers who bought the affected products should not eat them and should throw them away immediately. Full refunds are available by emailing RecallConcern@HotLineGlobal.com or calling 1-855-424-8390, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern. Questions about meat and poultry products can go to the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-674-6854.
